This first application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No.286/2023, dated 21.4.2024, registered at Police Station Kolar Road, District Bhopal (MP) for commission of offence under Sections 406, 409, 420, 120B, 34, 467,
468, 471 of IPC.
Applicant apprehending his arrest in connection with aforesaid offences has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. As per the prosecution case, G. R. Deshmukh and others lodged written complaint against present applicant and Prateek Rajan Saxena alleging that applicant received money from them on the pretext of construction of flats in the Kolar Road, Bhopal in the name and style of Janki Galaxy.

They received sale amount from the innocent purchasers but are not executing sale deeds of the flats Prateek Vats vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34507228/
1 in their favour.

sentences.text: It was also alleged that despite payment of full sale consideration builder and land owners have not constructed some of the apartments and have not handed over the possession and not executed the sale deed.
FIR was registered.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent.
He has not committed any offence.
He has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that applicant has handed over the possession and has also executed the sale deed in favour of the persons who had lodged FIR.
Dispute is of civil nature.
He has no criminal background.
Therefore, it is prayed that in the event of arrest, applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.

5. Learned counsel for the objector has submitted that except two objectors viz. Wilson Sonwani and Shilpi Sharma, sale deed have been executed in their favour and possession has also been handed over.
Therefore, it is submitted that anticipatory bail be not granted until and unless possession is handed over to the aforesaid two objectors also.

6. Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case including the fact that sale deed have already been executed in favour of objectors except two objectors, possession has also been handed over.
As per learned counsel for the applicant, possession will be handed over to these two objectors within a period of one month.

Considering the assurance given by learned counsel for the applicant but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which he may be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this first anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest applicant - Prateek Vats be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.

(iii) Applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;

(iv) In case, applicant is not arrested within a period of 10 days by the Investigation Officer, he shall surrender himself before the Investigation Officer within 15 days'
